items.title: Does the ROI of AI really only lie in corporate efficiencies?
items.excerpt: Nadim Sadek argues the book industry should acknowledge that AI can bring genuine value to human creativity, not just back-office efficiency.

items.title: Thélyson Orélien's Canadian publisher 'cuts ties' over AI allegations
items.excerpt: Les Editions du Boréal has cut all ties with the award-winning author of C'était ça ou mourir after finding evidence of AI use in his manuscript files.

items.title: SoA's position on generative AI 'remains unchanged' after backlash to Ethical AI Charter
items.excerpt: Society of Authors CEO Anna Ganley responded to member criticism of the Charter of Ethical AI Use in the Creative Industries, saying the SoA's stance on generative AI is unchanged.

items.title: Zachary Mason Chases the Ghost in the Machine
items.excerpt: In his speculative story collection, the computer scientist-novelist spins stories about relationships between humans and sentient AI.

items.title: Publishers Are Splitting on AI While the Ground Shifts Everywhere Else
items.excerpt: Meta claims AI rights to publisher content while Google pays; publishers are diverging on how to license and resist AI use of their work.

items.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated 'Odyssey'
items.excerpt: xAI's Grok released the opening minutes of its fully AI-generated adaptation of Homer's Odyssey; TechCrunch finds it passable but lacking artistry.

items.title: Kindle+ adds AI audiobooks. Royalty Share narrators wait
items.excerpt: With Kindle Unlimited rebranded as Kindle+, AI-voiced (Virtual Voice) audiobooks are included automatically while ACX narrators on Royalty Share deals are left out.

items.title: Publishers rely on trust, not tech, to ensure books aren't AI-generated
items.excerpt: Canadian publishers say no reliable tool detects AI-written books, so they lean on author disclosure and contract warranties after the Orélien affair.

items.title: WGAE Partners With AI-Shielding Tool Cloak
items.excerpt: WGA East members get free access to Cloak, software that makes documents unreadable to most AI models while preserving formatting for human readers.

items.title: Kyobo rejects suspicious 100,000-book order amid AI copyright fears
items.excerpt: Kyobo Book Centre turned down a bulk order from an overseas company amid fears Korean books are being bought en masse for AI training.

items.title: Were Korean authors' books used to train Claude?
items.excerpt: Books by Han Kang, Hwang Sok-yong and other Korean authors appear among works eligible for compensation in the Anthropic copyright settlement.

items.title: '부커상' 작가 로이 "AI에 내 장기를 적출 당했다"…앤트로픽 저작권 침해 비판
items.excerpt: 부커상 수상 작가 아룬다티 로이가 자신의 작품이 앤트로픽 AI 학습에 무단 사용됐다며 인간 창작의 존엄을 훼손하는 행위라고 비판했다.

items.title: kt Millie Seojae Introduces 'AI Briefing,' Which Understands Book Context
items.excerpt: Korean e-book subscription Millie's Library launched AI Briefing, an AI search that understands book, author and topic context and links straight into reading and recommendations.

items.title: 「LINEマンガ」、AIチャット「byUs」開始
items.excerpt: LINE Digital Frontier (Naver Webtoon) launched byUs, an AI story chat on LINE Manga that lets readers co-create new stories with officially licensed manga characters.

items.title: 'AI로 동화·웹툰 만들어요'…전국 어린이 AI 창작대회
items.excerpt: 어린이와 초등학생들이 AI를 활용해 동화·동요·웹툰을 직접 만드는 전국 어린이 AI 창작대회 본선이 열렸다.

items.title: "저작권 신탁기구 추진…AI의 '책 도둑질' 막아야"
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽의 국내 도서 대량 매입·해적판 학습 논란에 한국출판인회의가 저작권 신탁기구 추진과 정부·국회·AI 기업 대상 호소문을 내놨다.

items.title: Write a Novel in Thirty Days
items.excerpt: A bookseller weighs whether to stock AI-written novels with clear labelling, as machine-generated fiction tests the shop floor.
